title: What If a Mouse Fell Off a Skyscraper? Size Decides

scenes.text: What if a mouse fell off a skyscraper? A rat wouldn't walk away. A mouse might.
In 1926 the biologist J.B.S. Haldane wrote that a mouse can be dropped down a thousand-yard mine shaft and walk away.
A rat is killed, a man is broken, and a horse splashes. Same fall, different size.
Weight grows with volume, but air drag grows with surface area. Small bodies catch more air for their weight.
A mouse tops out near 25 miles an hour. A person falling flat reaches about 99. A horse, about 135.
So the mouse hits the ground gently, while the same height wrecks bigger animals. The estimates are calculated, never measured.

description:
What if a mouse fell off a skyscraper?
Air drag helps small bodies far more than big ones, so a mouse reaches a terminal speed near 25 miles an hour, while a person reaches about 99.
